stem: A scouting observation remains unresolved at shift change. What belongs in the handoff?
choices: Provide the most likely pest name so the receiving shift can act quickly.
Wait to document the issue until the diagnosis is final.
Record only that scouting was completed because the detailed observations remain in the source notes.
Hand off the location, evidence, incidence/severity or spatial pattern, containment actions, escalation status, and required follow-up without inventing a diagnosis.
rationale: An unresolved scouting issue still needs a decision-ready handoff. The next shift should know where the finding occurred, what was observed, how widespread or severe it appears, what containment or sanitation actions are active, and what follow-up is required. A guessed diagnosis or no written handoff weakens continuity.
